summary: Unit-tested the worldwide _format_phone change, which now uses phonenumbers 9.0.43 (listed in requirements.txt). The tests import server directly and make no network calls. New file tests/test_phone_worldwide.py has 115 cases, and all pass. Each of 31 international formats is run with default_cc 49 and with 91. Results: France '+33 06…'/'0033 6…' -> 33612345678. Italy '+39 06…' keeps the 0 -> 390612345678. Brazil gives 5511912345678. Nigeria '+234 0803…' -> 2348031234567. Australia '+61 0412…' -> 61412345678. Kenya '+254 0712…' -> 254712345678. Egypt '+20 010…' -> 201012345678. US (with parentheses and dashes) -> 14155552671. UK '+44 07700…' -> 447700900123. UAE '+971 050…' -> 971501234567. Malta, Lithuania (+ and 00) and Latvia are kept. Pakistan '+92 0300…' -> 923001234567. Bangladesh '+880 01712…' -> 8801712345678. Nepal gives 9779801234567. Germany '+49 0176…' -> 491761234567. India '+91 098765…' -> 919876543210. Oman 'p:+968…' and bidi-wrapped input are also handled. Bare numbers: 0176… -> 49176… with 49, and 10 digits -> 91… with 91. _clean_phone(raw,'berlin') returns '+intl' for all of these and '' for short bare numbers. The India _clean_phone path is unchanged: 10 digits for Indian numbers, +intl for other countries. _send_via_aisensy was run with httpx AsyncClient.post monkeypatched: the UC/Berlin key uses default 49 and the India key uses 91, and the destination is correct in both cases. Regression: the iteration 11-12 suite (test_berlin_phone_format.py) passes 50/50, and test_berlin_campaign_sync_e2e.py passes 2/2 (sync once, send_to_existing=false, sheets deleted by id). After the run: campaign_sheets=0, campaign_leads=0 and whatsapp_messages=0, so nothing was sent. GET /api/health returns healthy with database connected, and the backend logs show a clean startup. Ad-hoc probes also looked correct: Russia '+7 8 916…' -> 79161234567, Hungary '+36 06…' -> 36301234567, Argentina '+54 011 15…' -> 5491112345678, Netherlands '+31 06…' -> 31612345678, Indonesia, Turkey and China all fine.

minor.issue: There is no validity check. If phonenumbers says a number is not possible, the raw digits are returned unchanged. For example, '+0 123' -> '+0123' and '+49 01761234567890123' -> '+4901761234567890123'. Such leads are stored as valid and an AiSensy send would be tried. Consider marking them invalid when is_possible_number is False and the input had +/00.

A bare 10-digit foreign number written without +/00 (for example the Italian mobile '3331234567') gets 49 added -> 493331234567. This is expected with default 49, but the number is wrong. The sheet's data can't tell these apart.
'+52 1 55…' keeps the legacy mobile '1' -> 5215512345678. WhatsApp usually accepts this, so it is noted only.

action_items: Optional: treat numbers that phonenumbers says are not possible (and that had +/00) as invalid instead of returning raw digits
critical_code_review_comments: The fallback to raw digits when is_possible_number is False hides junk numbers. Return '' or flag them so the lead status becomes 'invalid'.
_send_via_aisensy at line ~3187 (the second send path) calls _format_phone(to_phone) with the default 91 even when it might be used for Berlin. Check that this path is only used for India.
server.py is about 5100 lines and should be split into modules.
seed_data_creation: The e2e regression created 2 TEST_ campaign sheets and deleted them by id through the API. Final counts: campaign_sheets 0, campaign_leads 0. No WhatsApp was sent.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && pytest tests/test_phone_worldwide.py tests/test_berlin_phone_format.py (unit, no network). The e2e needs REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL exported. It syncs once only; never re-sync an existing sheet, because that sends real AiSensy messages.
